messages:
olivia: Heads-up — customer (acct_8f3a) says when they apply a second promo via the API the original free-credit disappears instead of stacking. Repro on prod.

mike: Can you paste the exact curl + response / request ids?

olivia: Sure — simplified repro they ran:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/promos/apply \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***' \\  -d '{"account_id":"acct_8f3a","promo_code":"FREE100"}'
# returns 200 {"granted":100,"balance_key":"promo_balance"}
# then they call second promo
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/promos/apply -d '{"account_id":"acct_8f3a","promo_code":"BONUS50"}'
# returns 200 {"granted":50,"balance_key":"promo_balance"}
# Customer sees balance == 50 (not 150)
```

tara: Are these promos configured as stackable in the admin console? Also check if both grant_type=free_credit vs voucher. Historically vouchers were additive, free_credit sometimes overwritten.

olivia: In UI both flags look like "stackable: true". The customer also tried applying the second promo from the console and it stacked there, only API flow is broken (they said).

billing-bot: promo-service.log - INFO - applyPromo account=acct_8f3a promo=FREE100 grant=100 balance_key=promo_balance request_id=req_9a1
billing-bot: promo-service.log - INFO - applyPromo account=acct_8f3a promo=BONUS50 grant=50 balance_key=promo_balance request_id=req_9a2

mike: That log pattern suggests we upsert the same balance_key (promo_balance) instead of creating separate ledger entries per promo. If read path returns latest value instead of sum, customer would see overwrite.

tara: Agreed. Likely cause: backend stores promo grants in a map keyed by balance_key and not by (balance_key,promo_id). Admin console stacking code probably aggregates historical grants at read-time, while API write path is using an upsert API that replaced the entry.

kevin: Created internal ticket BILL-312 with repro steps and logs. @billing-eng please triage. Immediate mitigation: ask support to use the voucher attach endpoint for that account to preserve additive behavior: POST /v1/vouchers/attach {account_id, voucher_code}. That creates separate voucher ledger entries. Also I can run a one-off migration to convert the existing FREE100 grant into a voucher entry so the next apply won't replace it.

mike: Can we confirm there are no negative side effects if we convert existing grants to vouchers? Need to check expiry and usage semantics.

kevin: quick check: FREE100 expiry=2026-12-31, voucher conversion will preserve expiry & amount — we add a ledger entry and mark original promo as "migrated". No billing charges are affected. I'll run in staging first.

olivia: I told the customer: "We see the issue, engineering has a ticket (BILL-312). Short-term workaround: use the voucher attach API or apply the second promo from the console. We can also let us convert the first grant so you can successfully apply the second one now." They asked for ETA.

kevin: Targeting a patch in the next maintenance window (today + 48h) to change write semantics to append ledger entries per promo id. If that slips, we'll run a hotfix migration for affected accounts. Will update BILL-312 with ETA.

mike: Also add a test that simulates two stackable promotions applied via API to prevent regression.

tara: I'll add a unit/integration test and a note in the docs clarifying API vs console stacking behavior until this is fixed.

olivia: Customer OK with workaround for now. I'll follow up once BILL-312 has an ETA. Thanks everyone :white_check_mark:
